name: RxNav RxNorm API

provider.name: U.S. National Library of Medicine (Lister Hill Center)

summary: Keyless NLM API for RxNorm, the US normalized drug vocabulary: look up drugs by name, RxCUI or NDC, and walk ingredient, brand and dose-form relations.
description: RxNorm gives every clinical drug in the US market a concept id (RxCUI) and links it to ingredients, strengths, dose forms, brand names, NDC package codes and the drug vocabularies it was built from. The RxNav REST API resolves free-text or misspelled drug names to RxCUIs (approximate match and spelling suggestions), returns concept properties and all related concepts, and maps NDCs to concepts with their status history.

auth.notes: No key needed. A free UMLS (UTS) API key sent as Authorization: Bearer <key> raises the limit from 20 to 100 requests/second.

rate_limit.summary: No more than 20 requests per second per IP address (100 with a UTS API key); NLM recommends caching results for 12-24 hours.

endpoints.summary: Find the RxCUI for an exact drug name
Fuzzy match free-text or misspelled drug strings to RxCUIs
Clinical and branded drug products for an ingredient or brand name
All related concepts (ingredients, brands, dose forms, packs)
Status and history of an NDC package code
Spelling suggestions for a drug name

license.name: Free of charge under the NLM RxNav terms of service; content from some source vocabularies (e.g. SNOMED CT via RxClass) carries its own licence

coverage.temporal: Current RxNorm release, with concept and NDC history

agent_notes: Use the .json suffix (or Accept: application/json); without it responses are XML. Resolve names to an RxCUI first (rxcui.json for exact names, approximateTerm.json for messy input), then query /rxcui/{rxcui}/... for relations and properties. Prefer candidates with source RXNORM; /version.json reports the loaded release.
caveats: The drug-drug interaction API was discontinued; /REST/interaction/... returns 404.
Data is refreshed after each monthly RxNorm full release.
For bulk or high-rate use NLM points to RxNav-in-a-Box, a locally installable Docker version.
